meta.date: Before the crossing; Moroni writing after AD 400
meta.unit: The brother of Jared sees the Lord (Ether 3)
principles: A request that supplies its own solution
A body seen before it was taken
A record sealed in an unreadable language

world_behind.title: He answers the Lord's question with work
world_behind.text: Ether 2:25 asked what to prepare; verse 1 has him arrive with sixteen stones already molten.

world_behind.title: The count of vessels is given in a parenthesis
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says eight, inside a parenthesis. Ether 6:2 puts one stone in each end of each vessel, and this verse counts sixteen stones molten out of the rock, so the parenthesis is what makes that arithmetic close.

world_behind.title: He argues from weakness
world_behind.text: Verse 2 opens by naming his own weakness before God and the fallen nature of men. Ether 12:23 to 27 has Moroni make the same complaint about his writing and receive the answer that weakness is given so that men may be humble; the two passages sit nine chapters apart in the same book.

world_behind.title: The veil comes off at a touch
world_behind.text: Verse 6 has the Lord touch the stones and the brother of Jared see the finger. Ether 12:20 and 21 has Moroni cite this same moment as his leading example of faith, so the chapter is used as evidence inside the book that carries it.

world_behind.title: Two questions test him
world_behind.text: Verses 9 and 11 ask whether he saw more and whether he believes the words about to be spoken. The Lord asks him three questions in this chapter and Ether 2:23 and 25 had asked two more; five questions in two chapters is the densest run of divine questioning in the record.

world_behind.title: Moroni interrupts to explain
world_behind.text: Verses 17 through 20 step out to say what he can and cannot report. Ether 4:5 has him seal up the interpretation as well as the writing, and Ether 5:1 forbids a future translator to touch the sealed part. Moroni is describing a document he is holding and deliberately not transcribing.

world_behind.title: The account is sealed twice over
world_behind.text: Verses 22 through 24 seal the writing and the two stones, in a language no one can read.

words.text: The name of the mount, given because of its exceeding height. It appears once in the record and not in the King James Bible.
Melted and formed. Treated at 1 Nephi 17:9. The record uses the word six times, twice in this chapter, and the King James Bible thirty-nine.
Clear enough to see through. It appears once, here, in the record, and the King James Bible once, at Revelation 21:21. Verse 1 compares the stones to glass.
Surrounded on all sides. Treated at 2 Nephi 4:18. Three uses run through this record, with none in the King James Bible.
A curtain, and what separates men from God's presence. Treated at Alma 19:6. The word turns up seven times, three of them here, here, and the King James Bible forty-five.
A likeness. The record uses the word thirteen times and the King James Bible one hundred and one. Verse 15 says all men were created after his image in the beginning.
To make larger, or to make plain. Treated at Jacob 1:19. Its count is five times in this book, while the King James Bible nineteen. Verse 24 uses it of the two stones and the sealed writing.

phrases.term: Did molten out of a rock sixteen small stones
phrases.text: The answer to the question left standing at Ether 2:25. He brings a proposal rather than a repeated request.

phrases.term: Because of the fall our natures have become evil continually
phrases.text: His account of himself before he asks. The request comes after the confession.

phrases.term: Thou canst do this. We know that thou art able to show forth great power
phrases.text: Confidence stated flatly, right after the confession of weakness. Both are in the same prayer.

phrases.term: Which looks small unto the understanding of men
phrases.text: His guess at how the thing appears from outside. He is asking for sixteen glowing rocks.

phrases.term: I knew not that the Lord had flesh and blood
phrases.text: The reason for his fear, stated plainly. He had not expected a hand.

phrases.term: Never has man come before me with such exceeding faith as thou hast
phrases.text: The Lord's measure of him. Verse 15 restates it as never having shown himself to anyone before.
A question that opens a door. His answer in verse 10 is four words.

phrases.term: I am the Father and the Son
phrases.text: The declaration at the center of the chapter. Mosiah 15:2 had used the same pair of titles.

phrases.term: This body, which ye now behold, is the body of my spirit
phrases.text: The explanation of what he is seeing. Verse 16 adds that men were made after it.

phrases.term: He had faith no longer, for he knew, nothing doubting
phrases.text: Moroni's account of the change. Faith is described as ending in knowledge.

phrases.term: Ye shall write them in a language that they cannot be read
phrases.text: The seal built into the writing itself. Verse 24 says the stones will open it in due time.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: A count supplied in brackets and never used again
verses.text: The record interrupts its own opening sentence to give a number: "the brother of Jared, (now the number of the vessels which had been prepared was eight) went forth unto the mount." Nothing in the chapter depends on there being eight barges, and the parenthesis is the only place the fleet is counted. The construction is an editor's, not a narrator's, since a storyteller would have put the figure where the boats were built.

verses.label: v. 2–5
verses.title: A prayer that concedes before it asks
verses.text: The record has the petition open by granting the case against the petitioner: "we know that thou art holy and dwellest in the heavens, and that we are unworthy before thee; because of the fall our natures have become evil continually." Only after that does the request arrive, and it is specific about the mechanism: "touch these stones, O Lord, with thy finger, and prepare them that they may shine forth in darkness." Verse 5 supplies the argument for why the request is reasonable, and it is about scale: "thou art able to show forth great power, which looks small unto the understanding of men."

verses.label: v. 6–8
verses.title: A man explains his own fear by naming what he had wrong
verses.text: The record reports the collapse and then keeps the explanation: "I saw the finger of the Lord, and I feared lest he should smite me; for I knew not that the Lord had flesh and blood." The clause I knew not is a confession of an incorrect belief, made in the sentence that corrects it. Verse 7 has the question put to him first, "Arise, why hast thou fallen?", so the record establishes that an answer was asked for before giving one.

verses.label: v. 9–13
verses.title: An exchange kept as short turns
verses.text: The record preserves the conversation with almost nothing between the speeches. "Sawest thou more than this? And he answered: Nay; Lord, show thyself unto me." Then "Believest thou the words which I shall speak? And he answered: Yea, Lord, I know that thou speakest the truth, for thou art a God of truth, and canst not lie." Two questions and two answers, one of them four words long. The result follows immediately in verse 13 with no transition.

verses.label: v. 17–20
verses.title: The abridger steps in and says he is summarising
verses.text: The narrative stops and the compiler speaks in his own voice: "as I, Moroni, said I could not make a full account of these things which are written, therefore it sufficeth me to say that Jesus showed himself unto this man." Three verses then restate the episode in compressed form, "he ministered unto him even as he ministered unto the Nephites," and give the reason twice, "because of the knowledge of this man he could not be kept from beholding within the veil." The record tells the reader it is paraphrasing before it paraphrases.

chapter.title: He brings a proposal, not a complaint
chapter.text: Ether 2:25 left the question open and verse 1 answers it with sixteen finished stones. The work was done before the prayer.

chapter.title: Weakness and confidence sit in one prayer
chapter.text: Verse 2 confesses a fallen nature and verse 5 says plainly that the Lord can do this.

chapter.title: The request is modest and the result is not
chapter.text: He asked for light in boats and saw the Lord. The chapter turns on a small ask.

chapter.title: Fear comes from an unexpected fact
chapter.text: Verse 8 gives his reason: he had thought the Lord had no body. He was frightened by an anatomy.

chapter.title: A question opens the rest
chapter.text: Verse 9 asks whether he saw more, and verse 10 is four words that change everything.

chapter.title: Faith is described as ending
chapter.text: Verse 19 retires his faith at the moment he knew. Moroni treats knowledge as what faith is for.

chapter.title: The seal is in the language
chapter.text: Verse 22 has him write so it cannot be read, with stones provided to open it. Concealment and its remedy are given together.

chapter.title: The vision is total and withheld
chapter.text: Verse 25 shows him everyone who ever lived, and verse 27 has him seal it. Both happen in three verses.

applications.title: Bring something to work with
applications.text: He arrived with the stones already cut. Asking is stronger when you have done the part you could.

applications.title: Say your weakness and your confidence in the same breath
applications.text: He did both in one prayer. Neither cancels the other.

applications.title: Ask about the small thing
applications.text: He asked for light in boats. Where that led was not something he proposed.

applications.title: A question can be the kindness
applications.text: The response to a man face down in fear is "Arise, why hast thou fallen?" Being asked to account for a reaction is sometimes gentler than being talked out of it.

applications.title: Answer the follow-up question
applications.text: He was asked whether he saw more, and said show thyself. The second answer mattered more than the first.

applications.title: Say why you trust it
applications.text: Asked whether he believes what is about to be spoken, he answers that he knows it, because God is a God of truth and cannot lie. He supplies the ground of the trust and not only the fact of it.

applications.title: Not everything you receive is yours to publish
applications.text: He is told to treasure up what he has seen and heard and show it to no man until the appointed time. Being given something and being cleared to pass it on are separate grants.

applications.title: Expecting to be shown is part of the showing
applications.text: The verse says the Lord could not withhold anything from him, because he knew the Lord could show him all things. Expectation is described as a working part of the transaction.

questions.text: What have I asked for without doing the part I could?
Can I name my own weakness before I ask?
What do I believe God is able to do and never say so?
What have I assumed about God that turned out wrong?
Have I been asked whether I want more, and said no?
Where has my faith turned into knowing?
What have I been told to treasure up and not repeat?

entries.head: Ether 2:25

anchor.quote: did molten out of a rock sixteen small stones

entries.reason: the question he was sent away with, answered in stone

targets.quote: Therefore what will ye that I should prepare for you that ye may have light
targets.verse_text: And behold, I prepare you against these things; for ye cannot cross this great deep save I prepare you against the waves of the sea, and the winds which have gone forth, and the floods which shall come. Therefore what will ye that I should prepare for you that ye may have light when ye are swallowed up in the depths of the sea?
